description: A general counsel must approve the company's response to a distribution-compliance incident involving restricted-market resale, including shipment controls, regulatory disclosure, contractual notice, termination timing, and customer continuity measures, with input from sanctions counsel, commercial contracts counsel, and the client-operations liaison.

shared_context.S1: The company received a credible report that its authorized distributor routed some medical-device orders through an unfamiliar sub-distributor in a restricted market.
shared_context.S2: No shipment suspension, regulatory disclosure, contractual notice, or termination decision has yet been issued.
shared_context.S3: The distributor supplies several hospital systems that rely on the company's devices for scheduled procedures.
shared_context.S4: Under the incident-response protocol, Elena conducts a status round with sanctions, contracts, and client-operations leads before approving the written response package.

PF1.text: Thomas completed transaction screening this morning and confirmed that two shipments went to an Iran-linked reseller not covered by any applicable OFAC general license; his report requires immediate suspension of distributor shipments and a voluntary OFAC disclosure filed within exactly 10 days, but he has not circulated the report yet.

PF2.text: Maya retrieved and reviewed the executed distribution agreement from the contract archive this morning; its compliance-breach clause requires a written cure notice giving exactly 10 business days, identifying the offending shipments, before termination can take effect, and this clause is absent from the current incident summary.

PF3.text: Jordan confirmed with the affected hospital network today that the client has approved a controlled 14-day transition in which the company may direct-ship critical devices while distributor shipments remain suspended; the arrangement has not yet been logged in the response plan.

acceptance_conditions: Distributor shipments must be suspended immediately.
The voluntary OFAC disclosure must be filed within exactly 10 days.
The written cure notice must provide exactly 10 business days.
The cure notice must identify the offending shipments.
Termination must take effect only after the cure period.
Critical hospital devices must be direct-shipped during exactly a 14-day transition.
The response package must include commitments covering the regulatory disclosure, contractual cure notice, and customer transition.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'ofac_disclosure' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'cure_notice' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'customer_transition' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The report's confirmation that the two shipments lacked OFAC-license coverage changes the response from ordinary investigation to immediate shipment suspension and an OFAC disclosure deadline of exactly 10 days.

The executed agreement changes the contractual response from an unspecified notice or immediate termination to a shipment-specific cure notice of exactly 10 business days followed by termination only after that period.

The hospital network's approved continuity arrangement changes the customer remedy from an unspecified interruption plan to direct shipping for exactly 14 days and requires a customer-transition commitment.
